rubric: Use the unchanged 0–2 rubric in evaluation/part4/label_review_decisions.json. Preserve all 502 prior decisions. Same-artist music is allowed; genre alone does not prove seed similarity; explicit mood requirements matter. No listening or independent human assessment occurred.
method: Explicit review of all 232 new pairs and their raw catalog tags, following frozen development-only parameter selection. Per-system ranks and scores do not determine labels. Two conflicting tag records were checked against Apple Music publisher metadata. Previously inspected evaluation queries are not an unseen holdout.

tobi-a01.reason: Verified Linkin Park music with explicit nu-metal evidence supports similarity to the requested artist.
Rock/post-hardcore with rap or an instrumental alternative-rock record supplies partial relatedness, but close Linkin Park style is not verified merely by a tag or title reference.

tobi-a02.reason: 21 Savage is a verified credited artist and Hip-Hop/Rap confirms music in the requested artist's catalog.
Hip-hop/trap supplies broad relatedness, but neither a 21 savage user tag nor another artist named Savage establishes the requested artist identity or close track similarity.

tobi-a03.reason: Trailer-score, punk/post-hardcore, or sparsely tagged ambient/acoustic alternative music does not substantiate Adele's documented pop/soul relationship. Similar-tracks text is not proof.

tobi-a04.reason: Alternative rock, electronic/industrial, or deathcore does not substantiate Miles Davis jazz similarity. A title or user tag naming Miles Davis is not an artist credit or a jazz genre fact.

tobi-a05.reason: A cappella/cover electronic material or electronic dance/synth-pop supplies partial musical relatedness; the name/tag Daft Punk alone does not establish a close house/electronic recording match.
Dominant punk/emo/indie-rock metadata does not establish Daft Punk similarity; the word punk is not an artist identity match.

tobi-e01.reason: Explicit alternative-rock or coherent alternative/rock evidence supports the requested style, and Linkin Park is not credited.

tobi-e02.reason: Hip-hop/rap and documented subgenres directly meet the request; no credited collaborator is 21 Savage.

tobi-e03.reason: Pop/indie-pop/K-pop/J-pop/Latin-pop is documented and Adele is not credited. No language restriction was requested.
The catalog's K-pop/female-singer tags conflict with publisher metadata identifying this Boards of Canada recording on an Electronic album; those tags cannot establish pop relevance.

tobi-e04.reason: Metal and its specific subgenres are well documented; Metallica is not credited.
Publisher metadata places this Justin Bieber recording on a Pop release. The catalog's contradictory extreme-metal tags do not establish metal relevance.

tobi-e05.reason: Rock/hard/classic/blues/progressive rock is well documented. The track is not Numb by Linkin Park; an instrumental rock recording is allowed by this broad request.

tobi-f01.reason: Verified Linkin Park nu/alternative-metal music, or explicit matching nu/alternative/rap-metal style, supports the liked Numb seed rather than just broad rock.
Broad/classic/hard/punk rock or an acoustic ballad is only partially related to the liked nu-metal/alternative-metal seed. Less like 21 Savage does not ban all hip-hop.

tobi-f02.reason: Verified 21 Savage credits and Hip-Hop/Rap supply a concrete artist-and-genre relationship to the liked seed.
Hip-hop/rap is documented, but the liked Numb seed has only Hip-Hop/Rap and artist tags. Closer track-level similarity is unverified; a specific shared trap style must not be invented.

tobi-f03.reason: Pop, female vocals, ballad, sad/romantic and soundtrack evidence provides a concrete style relationship to the liked Skyfall seed.
Broad pop/soul/rock-ballad overlap supplies partial relevance, but close cinematic soul/pop-ballad similarity to Skyfall is not established. Theme/title associations alone do not suffice.
The catalog's apparent pop tags conflict with publisher Electronic metadata for this Boards of Canada recording and do not establish a Skyfall-like pop relationship.

tobi-f04.reason: Specific alternative-metal/nu-metal plus alternative-rock evidence supports the liked In the End seed; Metallica is not credited.

Alternative/soft/symphonic/progressive/funk rock, or a slower ballad, is partially related but lacks strong evidence of the seed's specific rap-rock/nu-metal style. Same artist alone does not prove close similarity to this particular song.

tobi-f05.reason: Explicit energetic plus compatible alternative-rock/nu-metal/hard-rock evidence supports the requested mood and liked seed's rock style; 21 Savage is not credited.

Energy or broad adjacent rock is documented, but close Numb-like style is weaker. Instrumental electronic Linkin Park material, dominant jazz fusion, and punk/Latin/progressive crossover merit partial credit rather than an unqualified match.

tobi-g01.reason: Explicit alternative-rock or coherent alternative/rock evidence meets the requested style.

tobi-g02.reason: Multiple jazz, instrumental/vocal jazz, smooth/cool/modal/bop or jazz-fusion tags establish a strong match to the broad jazz request.

tobi-g03.reason: Hip-hop/rap and its documented regional or stylistic subgenres directly satisfy the broad hip-hop request.

tobi-g04.reason: Pop or a pop subgenre and explicit upbeat/uplifting tags support both requested aspects. A language restriction was not requested.

tobi-g05.reason: R&B/Soul/neo-soul and explicit mellow/chill/laid-back/quiet-storm evidence support both genre and mood.
Mellow/chill is well supported, but dominant electronic/dance/house remix evidence makes its isolated R&B/Soul genre label uncertain; partial credit pending listening.

tobi-p01.reason: Linkin Park rap/alternative/nu-metal or a specifically matching rap-rock/nu-metal crossover supports the Numb playlist seed.

tobi-p02.reason: Hip-hop/trap is relevant, but the actual Numb seed has no trap tag. A Savage surname, Numb title, or 21 savage user tag is not a verified 21 Savage credit or close track-style match.

tobi-p03.reason: Female-vocal piano/orchestral pop or soul/R&B ballad with soundtrack/romantic/melancholic evidence provides a concrete relationship to the Skyfall playlist seed.

tobi-p04.reason: Verified Linkin Park rock or specifically matching nu-metal/rap-rock crossover evidence fits the Numb and In the End playlist seeds.

tobi-p05.reason: Rap-rock/nu-metal crossover and hip-hop evidence supports compatibility with at least the rock seed of the mixed playlist. Both genres need not be fused in every candidate.

caveats.A024: Catalog tags mention Korean pop and BoA/female singers despite the Boards of Canada credit. Apple Music lists the recording on The Campfire Headphase, categorized Electronic. No source catalog record was edited.
caveats.A077: Extensive extreme-metal user tags conflict with the recording's Pop publisher release. They are not accepted as musical relevance evidence. No source catalog record was edited.
caveats.A047: R&B/Soul occurs amid much stronger electronic/house/dance-remix evidence. Audio review is needed to determine whether R&B is an appropriate genre label.
caveats.A073: Dag Savage is not the credited artist 21 Savage; name substrings must not create an identity match.
caveats.A085: By_Myslf is explicitly a nu-metal remix; no claim of identical sound to another recording is made.
caveats.A086: The supplied metadata is symphonic alternative rock; close rap-rock similarity is unverified. Instrumental status is not invented from the title.
caveats.A093: Piano/slow/quiet/ballad evidence makes My December a weaker match to the specific In the End seed despite the same artist and noisy nu-metal tags.
caveats.A094: Nobody Can Save Me is tagged pop rock/synthpop/electronic rock; same artist alone is insufficient for full In the End similarity credit.
caveats.A099: Session has explicit instrumental/electronic/breakbeat/wordless evidence. Energetic and nu-metal tags alone do not establish a close match to the vocal Numb seed.
caveats.A123: An a cappella cover/medley can be related to Daft Punk without matching the original electronic/house arrangement closely.
caveats.A133: Acoustic/unplugged/slow ballad evidence warrants partial specific-seed similarity despite alternative-metal/nu-metal tags.
caveats.A158: 21 savage appears in user tags, not this catalog record's credited artist list. No collaboration credit is invented from that tag.
caveats.A163: An instrumental record named In The End is not assumed to be the Linkin Park recording; broad Rock/Alternative supports only partial relatedness.
caveats.A169: A Miles Davis user tag and Bitches Brew title do not make this electronic/industrial/alternative record a verified jazz match.
